verdict_scope: Non-author correctness and static design review; not performance, native behavior, product gate or default adoption
findings: Successful receipt stores max(parser.nodes, validator.work), since each pre-existing counter separately compares against max_nodes; no budget charging/diagnostic branch was changed.

fits_limits requires no diagnostics, full token tape including EOF <= max_tokens, and receipt <= max_nodes. EOF can cause conservative rejection even when the original lexer succeeds, but fallback preserves original result rather than inventing an error.

Only max_tokens and max_nodes are neutralized, under a new domain-separated private Parse identity. Source bytes/path/FileId/ModuleId, nine remaining limit axes, build_inputs and rule/schema/producer identity stay bound. Driver always uses the unchanged default attribute context.
Untrusted public ParseResult/ParseUsage values have no insertion path into private raw snapshots; no decoder or disk syntax cache was added.
Insufficient existing success receipt selects the original full-budget key and original parser. Existing fallback entries can be reused only under their exact original quotas.

Loader and project_pipeline both select parse_key with matching effective token/node quotas. Source byte validation and project token/EOF charging still execute; all current filesystem import resolutions, missing/ambiguous file checks and source reads remain live.

Single-source downstream phases derive their keys from a separate original full identity, not the neutral Parse key. Project downstream phases also retain full project identity. Disk source backup and frontend checkpoint identities are unchanged.
Only successful raw parses are published; independent Verify, cancellation boundaries, active-query cleanup and capacity eviction behavior remain intact.
limits: Private raw query reuse is not a full syntax/semantic incremental compiler; later phases remain live under their current identities.
Parse query event Reused/Executed is not itself an actual lexer invocation counter because discovery may provide a checked Arc after capacity eviction.
Tests do not import CP22/CP26 performance or disk publication conclusions; no old timing is attributed to CP33.
CP33 is based on ee72fd6 and does not contain CP29/CP32. No joint-candidate behavior or speed has been established.
All code remained frozen; no test duration is a performance sample.
